title: R13-R15 CLASSES resource-bound architecture and cross-reader review
mode: Authoritative local ODA specification review, current-source audit, and primary-source peer comparison
supersedes: The earlier crosswalk wording that described dwgReader15 as having an explicit class-count ceiling; that wording was inaccurate.
scope: Determine whether LibreDWG's R13-R2000 class-count resource advisory has a direct equivalent in libdxfrw.
Verify the R13-R15 CLASSES wire layout against the authoritative ODA specification and current reader implementation.
Refine PAR-14 readiness without adding a speculative class-count cap, redundant test, or support claim.

sources.project: Open Design Alliance Open Design Specification for .dwg files 5.4.1
sources.revision: Local authoritative PDF; sections 10.1 (R13-R15) and 10.2 (R18+), reviewed 2026-10-20.
sources.observed: Section 10.1 gives an RL class-data byte size followed by repeated BS/TV/B class records and says records are read until the data is exhausted; it does not define a num_classes field. Section 10.2 adds the R18+ maximum class number field. This establishes the version distinction; it does not prescribe libdxfrw's resource policy.
sources.limits: No DWG parse body was changed. The PDF wins over third-party descriptions for wire-format semantics.

sources.revision: Public advisory reviewed 2026-10-20; affected versions <0.14, fixed in 0.14.
sources.observed: The advisory attributes its R13-R2000 DoS to a crafted num_classes value driving per-iteration realloc in LibreDWG's decode_R13_R2000 without a sanity check.
sources.limits: Peer-specific implementation failure; it is not evidence of a matching libdxfrw defect.

sources.observed: The reader bounds class iteration by a computed section-data end bit, applies a class-number range check, and reads the explicit maximum-class-number field on AC1018+. It preserves parsed entries in order.
sources.limits: Independent implementation comparison only. Its signed class-number type, range policy, and parser behavior are not normative and do not qualify libdxfrw.

sources.project: C++ working draft, unordered associative container requirements
sources.observed: The standard specifies average-case fast retrieval but permits linear worst-case operations (quadratic for some aggregate operations). This supports considering a direct-index duplicate set over the local finite 16-bit ID domain if profiling justifies it.
sources.limits: A standards-level complexity bound does not prove that attacker-controlled class IDs produce a slow case on any particular standard-library implementation.

observed: The reader admits an RL-declared class-data size only after checking MaxBufferSize and the enclosing physical range, copies that exact payload, and parses until its byte boundary rather than trusting a class-count field.

DRW_Class::classNum is uint16_t and is decoded from BS. The reader rejects IDs below 500 and duplicate IDs. Thus at most 65,036 distinct newly accepted IDs are representable in the range 500..65,535; this is a representation-domain bound, not an explicit format count or policy cap.

DRW_Class::parseDwg reads mandatory BS, variable-text, and bit fields; the caller rejects a failed or invalid cursor and records per-record bit ranges, but it does not explicitly compare dataRangeEnd > dataRangeStart. No successful zero-progress path was identified in this fixed parser sequence; a monotonic-cursor assertion would be defense-in-depth rather than a fix for the peer's count/realloc root cause.

Staging uses a vector, an unordered map for duplicate detection, class strings converted to UTF-8, and coverage metadata. The raw section bound makes these allocations finite, but no tight aggregate decoded-memory budget was established in this pass.
localCrosswalk.classification: DIFFERENT_ARCHITECTURE for the peer's num_classes/per-iteration-realloc trigger; CONDITIONAL_RESOURCE_PROFILE for any future aggregate-memory-policy change; OPTIONAL_PERF_HARDENING for a direct-index class-ID duplicate set.

planChanges: Corrected the parity plan and prior crosswalk receipt: dwgReader15 has no explicit class-count field or count ceiling; R13-R15 class iteration is bounded by the RL payload and duplicate-free uint16 class-ID domain.
Closed the specific LibreDWG class-count advisory as a different-architecture peer analog; did not add an arbitrary cap, synthetic num_classes control, or external sample.

Added an implementation-ready optional optimization: if a generated scaling probe shows worthwhile gain, replace stagedMap's duplicate-only membership role with a fixed 65,536-bit seen set while retaining the existing published-classes collision check.

Separated any aggregate decoded-memory review from the class-count advisory and made it conditional on shared MaxBufferSize changes or measured resource pressure; account for the raw copy, transient text buffers, UTF-8 strings, class objects, coverage rows, and indexes.
Retained fast generated controls only for an actual implementation change, the existing infrequent full-suite cadence, self-unblocking, and no support promotion.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-14: distinguish peer count-field attacks from local section-payload-bounded legacy parsing.
PAR-14: do not add speculative class-count limits; consider deterministic direct-index duplicate checks only if generated scaling measurements justify it.
PAR-14: profile aggregate decoded memory separately if the global section-size policy changes or resource evidence warrants it.
